adjudication_note:
The concept that had nowhere to land. A fresh adversarial reviewer found `technical.repo`'s automatic form `recompra` firing on a fund's own share BUYBACK — `o valor de recompra da cota`, `o volume de recompra das cotas do fundo` — and rewriting it to `operação compromissada`, a money-market repurchase agreement, which is a different instrument entirely. 5 wrong of about 12 bare occurrences, roughly 42 %.

Under this campaign's rule that is the FORBID case, not the demote case: below 50 % the form stays automatic and the wrong collocations are forbidden. But forbidding alone would leave the buyback with no concept at all, turning a wrong match into a silent gap. So the sense is registered here and the collocations are forbidden in amendment 68 — the two operations only work together.

The reviewer also found `Cambial` unregistered. That one stings: the amendment that fixed `Multimercado` named its three siblings in its own reasoning — `Renda Fixa`, `Ações`, `Cambial` — and I checked neither of the other two. `Renda Fixa` and `Ações` resolve; `Cambial` did not, in any of its 4 occurrences. Naming a taxonomy in a justification is not the same as checking it.

concepts.def: A fund buying back its own shares from holders, which CVM 175 conditions on the buyback price relative to net asset value. Unrelated to a repurchase agreement, which is `technical.repo`.
The CVM 175 fund category whose principal risk factor is foreign-exchange variation, the fourth of the four categories beside Renda Fixa, Ações and Multimercado.
